[[File:Evan Lorentz DecipherCon 2002.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Head judge, Star Trek CCG Worlds, [[DecipherCon 2002]]. Photo: Decipher.]]
'''Evan Lorentz''' ("Mot the Barber") was a Decipher game designer. He is credited on Decipher's [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] team (2001): the rulebook credits list him by name, with no role, under "The Decipher Jedi Knights Team".<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Credits: "THE DECIPHER JEDI KNIGHTS TEAM: Tom Lischke (lead game designer); ... Dean Irwin; Evan Lorentz; Rich Loftus; ..." Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref> He also designed for Decipher's ''[[Star Trek CCG]]'' and ''Austin Powers'' CCG, and co-hosted ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]''.

== Star Trek CCG player and Ambassador ==
Lorentz, of Littleton, Colorado, became a ''Star Trek CCG'' Ambassador in December 1996, one of the first. He was known in the Star Trek CCG community as "Mot the Barber", author of the "Useless" Card Reviews and a Borg specialist.<ref name="amb" /> He won the 1998 GenCon Open and was the only player that year to qualify for the Star Trek CCG World Championships with a Borg deck. He said he had written over 100 strategy articles on the game.<ref name="bio">[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/specialevents/current/regionalqualifiers/lorentzbio.htm Star Trek CCG World Championships 1998 finalists: Evan Lorentz], Decipher (1998). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990507083701/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/specialevents/current/regionalqualifiers/lorentzbio.htm Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher published his 1998 World Finals deck, "The Killer B's".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/specialevents/98worldfinals/decks/evanlorentzdeck.htm The Killer B's, by Evan Lorentz], Decipher, Star Trek CCG 1998 World Finals deck lists. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990424150645/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/specialevents/98worldfinals/decks/evanlorentzdeck.htm Internet Archive]</ref>

== DecipherCon 1999 ==
[[DecipherCon 1999]] ran 11–14 November 1999. Decipher's ''Radio Free Decipher'' feeds there included "Evan Lorentz, AP designer, tells all" (Thursday) and "Evan's thoughts on Round 1 of ST finals" (Saturday).<ref name="thu">[http://www1.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Thursday], Decipher (1999). Listing: "Evan Lorentz, AP designer, tells all (M. Tuttle, E. Lorentz) 4:40mins". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010217093703/http://www1.decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/THU/index.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="sat">[http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html DecipherCon 1999 audio feeds: Saturday], Decipher (1999). Listing: "Evan's thoughts on Round 1 of ST finals (M. Tuttle, E. Lorentz) 0:50mins". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000313011020/http://decipher.com:80/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/audiofeeds/SAT/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> A Decipher photograph shows him and Super Vol [[Kim Burns]] briefing ''Star Wars Insider'' writer [[Richard Handley]] on the Star Trek CCG World Finals.<ref name="fri26">[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/FRI/fri26.html DecipherCon 1999 Friday photo fri26], Decipher (1999). Caption: "Evan Lorentz and Super Vol Kim Burns tell Star Wars Insider writer Richard Handley what's happening with the Star Trek CCG World Finals". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000612184011/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/photos/FRI/fri26.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Star Trek CCG design ==
In 2000 Lorentz wrote "The Amazing Morphing Icon" for Decipher's ''The Trouble With Tribbles'' expansion pages, on the history of the original-series icon.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/expansions/thetroublewithtribbles/062000lorentzarticle.html The Amazing Morphing Icon], Evan Lorentz, Decipher (2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000903031329/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/expansions/thetroublewithtribbles/062000lorentzarticle.html Internet Archive]</ref> In August 2000 Decipher reported that Lorentz, who had answered Star Trek CCG rules questions, had moved to another position at Decipher.<ref>[http://www.trektoday.com/news/220800_05.shtml News Bullets], TrekToday (22 August 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20000919181718/http://www.trektoday.com:80/news/220800_05.shtml Internet Archive]</ref> In 2002 he wrote design logs for the ''Star Trek CCG'' Second Edition as "Evan Lorentz, Game Designer".<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/startrek/expansions/secondedition/111902lorentzdesign1.html How CCGs Are Like Ice Cream Parlors], Evan Lorentz, Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021203010212/http://www.decipher.com:80/startrek/expansions/secondedition/111902lorentzdesign1.html Internet Archive]</ref>

At [[DecipherCon 2002]] he and [[Tim Ellington]] were billed for the Star Trek CCG Design-a-card Seminar. The Daily News report has Lorentz and [[Brad DeFruiter|Brad De Fruiter]], "Star Trek CCG's intrepid designers", presenting it for Second Edition.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/events/eventdescother.html DecipherCon 2002 event descriptions: non-tournament events], Decipher (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20030204113713/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2002/events/eventdescother.html Internet Archive]</ref><ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102stcarddesign1.html Star Trek CCG Design-a-card Seminar: Part 1], Decipher, DecipherCon 2002 Daily News (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021221151700/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2002/reports/1102stcarddesign1.html Internet Archive]</ref> He gave Second Edition demos,<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103stccgdemos.html Boldly Going Into Second Edition: Star Trek CCG Demos], Decipher, DecipherCon 2002 Daily News (2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20021107102250/http://www.decipher.com:80/deciphercon/2002/reports/1103stccgdemos.html Internet Archive]</ref> and he judged the Star Trek CCG World Championship final.<ref name="dc02stand" />

== Radio Free Decipher ==
Lorentz co-hosted ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' with [[Kyle Heuer]] in 2002 and hosted later episodes himself. As a ''Star Trek'' CCG designer he discussed the ''Motion Pictures'' expansion, and he helped proofread the foreign-language ''Lord of the Rings'' TCG press sheets.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=36s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 00:36. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8aNpe-I-KQk&t=1148s Broadcast 110 - Radio Free Decipher (11 January, 2002): SWCCG Player's Committee, ST/LOTR News], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 19:08. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8aNpe-I-KQk Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 110 transcript]].</ref>

== Austin Powers CCG ==
On a March 2002 episode of Radio Free Decipher, Lorentz said he had "a pretty heavy hand in the design" of Decipher's ''Austin Powers'' CCG. The same episode previewed the ''Star Trek'' CCG ''Motion Pictures'' expansion, for which he explained the renaming of the Excelsior icon as the Classic Films icon.<ref name="rfd119">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KvLjZofZcY&t=750s Broadcast 119 - Radio Free Decipher (15 March, 2002): Chris and MaryGail Coffee on SWCCG Open], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 12:30. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8KvLjZofZcY Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 119 transcript]].</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8KvLjZofZcY&t=345s Broadcast 119 - Radio Free Decipher (15 March, 2002): Chris and MaryGail Coffee on SWCCG Open], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 05:45. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-8KvLjZofZcY Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 119 transcript]].</ref> Decipher had already billed him as "AP designer" at DecipherCon 1999.<ref name="thu" />
